body:
vim_na_cfuncs.txt lists Vim C functions that are N/A to Nvim. Based on 'src/proto/*.proto' files.
Whitelist version.c for now.

---------

Next step is reviewing doc files for files that are mostly N/A but it contains at least 1 function we kept/renamed/refactored  (ie. term.c) .

---------

~~Need help.~~ It's ~~too slow and~~ is reliant on `git diff` detecting the C "symbols" (via regex?) so there could be min. version Git requirement. v2 for https://github.com/git/git/commit/8a2e8da367f7175465118510b474ad365161d6b1 ?
`-U0` is to increase the likelihood that each hunk is linked to a C (function) symbol.

~~Maybe it's time for the lua refactor just to reduce the child processes/shells but the pattern files and diff have to based on Nvim's internal diff and patterns.~~

It should find N/A patches since version v9, specifically v9.0.0515.
Temporarily modify `list_vim_commits()` to start on tag v9.0.0000 or later to get to the expected list.

Sample N/A patches:

```
vim-patch:495282b6e Correct list of patch numbers
vim-patch:85d9b03f8 Correct list of patches.
vim-patch:8.2.2598: Vim9: :open does not need to be supported
vim-patch:9.0.0014: missing part of the test override change
vim-patch:9.0.0515: virtual text highlight starts too early when 'number' is set
vim-patch:9.0.0516: virtual text "above" highlights gap after it
vim-patch:9.0.0518: virtual text highlight starts too early with 'nowrap'
vim-patch:9.0.1124: virtual text at a column position is truncated
vim-patch:9.0.1463: virtual text truncation only works with Unicode 'encoding'
vim-patch:9.0.1482: crash when textprop has a very large "padding" value
vim-patch:9.0.1695: Crash with overlong textprop above
vim-patch:c49cb93a8 patch 9.1.1392: missing patch number
vim-patch:9.1.1397: tabpanel not correctly updated on :tabonly
vim-patch:9.1.1530: Missing version change in v9.1.1529
vim-patch:9.1.1982: Use after free with redraw_listener_add()
```

I intended to skip diffs that only move files or contain hunks with C symbols.
Limiting the patterns to applicable files even if documented in `:h vim-diff` to not waste reviewer time.

~~If the shell script is rewritten, then we can add more patterns or target different C symbols or non-C symbols.~~

comment_data.body: `^` should be safe under Vim's current code style (unless they have exceptions due to `#ifdefs`) .

The risk with this strat is marking applicable **NEW** code (ie. functions, arrays, typedef) under N/A functions/arrays as N/A but it hasn't happened yet because I'm relying non '*.c" files for the applicable code.

How often does this happen for a vim-patch to contain only new "C" code?

-    grep '^<')" || true
+    grep '^<' | sed 's/^< //')" || true
   test -z "$FILES_REMAINING" && return 0
-  if test "$FILES_REMAINING" == "$(printf "< src/version.c\n")"; then
-    local VERSION_LNUM
-    VERSION_LNUM=$(git -C "${VIM_SOURCE_DIR}" diff-tree --no-commit-id --numstat -r "$patch" -- src/version.c | grep -c '^2\s\+0')
-    test "$VERSION_LNUM" -ne 1 && return 1
-    local VERSION_VNUM
-    VERSION_VNUM="$(git -C "${VIM_SOURCE_DIR}" diff-tree --no-commit-id -U1 -r "$patch" -- src/version.c |
-      grep -Pzc '[ +]\/\*\*\/\n\+\s+[0-9]+,\n[ +]\/\*\*\/\n')" || true
-    test "$VERSION_VNUM" -eq 1 && return 0
-  fi
-  return 1
+
+  C_FILES=$(echo "$FILES_REMAINING" | grep '.*\.c$')
+  test "$FILES_REMAINING" != "$C_FILES" && return 1
+
+  local VERSION_LNUM VERSION_VNUM
+  for file in $C_FILES; do
+    HUNKS=$(git -C "${VIM_SOURCE_DIR}" diff-tree --no-commit-id -U0  -r "$patch" -- "$file" | grep -P '^@@ .* @@')

+      HUNK_NUM_FINAL=$(echo "$HUNKS" | sed 's/^@@ .* @@ \?//' | grep -cv -f "$NA_HUNKS_C")

comment_regular_data.body:
> there could be min. version Git requirement.

that's fine. 


is `git log -L` could be useful? it shows the history of a given function.

       -L<start>,<end>:<file>, -L:<funcname>:<file>
           Trace the evolution of the line range given by <start>,<end>, or by
           the function name regex <funcname>, within the <file>.

I don't see `git log -L` working with my proposed strategy.

It should be treated as a new strategy, `list_na_patches_from_function_file`, to investigate specific N/A patches based on the given specific function and file instead of cycling through all unmerged patches.

https://github.com/git/git/commit/be58e70dbadf3cb3f4aa5829d513d886ae8bc460 . Git v1.6.1+ is the min version? Or Git v2.0.0 for commit https://github.com/git/git/commit/8a2e8da367f7175465118510b474ad365161d6b1 ?

```
diff --git a/src/version.c b/src/version.c
index 779e11696..50660311d 100644
--- a/src/version.c
+++ b/src/version.c
@@ -706,0 +707,2 @@ static int included_patches[] =
+/**/
+    2174,
@@ -710,0 +713,2 @@ static int included_patches[] =
+/**/
+    2171,
```

Could change vim_na_cfuncs.txt to scan for arrays to validate version.c hunks. Next PR. Likely need Git v2.0.0. minimum but is there is a supported OS that runs Git v1?

> Likely need Git v2.0.0. minimum but is there is a supported OS that runs Git v1?

if it's only for local tooling, we don't need to worry about that. as long as it isn't required to build `nvim`. and Git v2 is 10+ years old anyway

This is an important util, because going forward we should be very, very aggressive about declining the vast majority of legacy Vim's work. They simply aren't that relevant anymore, and I have low confidence in most of the changes they are making.

I have an upcoming docs change which will change the vim-patch policy to an "allowlist" instead of a "denylist", i.e. we will explicitly choose which (very few) modules/topics Vim still "owns".

I also think we should decline most of their docs changes at this point.

Allowlist can start on certain files that are barely applicable due to few functions (ie. src/term.c). Should be gradual if the low confidence is due to "recent" Vim 9.x patches. Vim eval, ex-commands, autocmds should remain relevant even if cherry-picking them from Vim9 is tedious.

Unsure if an allowlist will make maintenance easier since I am relying on the denylist to determine the applicable files.
I don't plan on creating/prioritizing the allowlist until I hit a dead end with the denylist strategy.

> I don't see `git log -L` working with my proposed strategy.
> 
> It should be treated as a new strategy, `list_na_patches_from_function_file`, to investigate specific N/A patches based on the given specific function and file instead of cycling through all unmerged patches.

I tried again with

```
git -C .vim-src show -B10 -L ':completing_value:src/optionstr.c' v9.2.0764
```

but it omits the relevant `#ifdef` change by ignoring `-B10` (or  `-U100`). It doesn't return the "exact context" I need compared to a regular diff hunk.

-----------

If this PR wasn't merged, I was considering the following:

- `#ifdef` scanning as well to eliminate `#ifdef` only patches that are most likely N/A (especially if you ignore whitespace).
- N/A functions related `t_` options ( `src/term.c`?)
- N/A code based on `:h dev-vimpatch` (`src/alloc.c`)

but code analysis on the actual changes is more experimental than blacklisting N/A functions from `src/proto/*` because it can convert N/A code to applicable code.

> I also think we should decline most of their docs changes at this point.

I can't determine which of the remaining runtime/doc/*.vim are relevant but git can (be configured to) parse Vimscript and Vimdoc help files for diff headers. We can reuse this strat for N/A `runtime/doc/*.txt` patches, specifically the datetime/release 1-liner changes per Vim release.
